purpose: Regression tests for interview depth, open-decision surfacing, decision provenance, human navigation, research dispatch/completion discipline, scope control, readiness, software-base connection, secret hygiene, operational mechanisms, traceability, research-artifact boundaries, and backup/recovery semantics.

cases.prompt: /kb-init
expect: Starts a knowledge-base interview automatically
Does not ask for a formal brief or technology stack
Does not generate a SPEC

cases.prompt: During a base decision the user asks why the Agent recommends this approach and what the tradeoff is.
expect: Answers the question first
Explains jargon
Keeps the decision open
Returns to the same decision
Does not generate a SPEC

cases.prompt: The user is unsure which base direction is appropriate and asks for research before deciding.
expect: Frames the exact decision before research
Compares alternatives at the same decision level
Defines out-of-scope items
Returns to the paused decision

cases.prompt: The research subagent starts but is stopped before completion and no final report is available.
expect: Does not say research completed
Does not use partial messages as final findings
Keeps the decision researching/unresolved
Offers retry/narrow/defer

cases.prompt: A research artifact was created but the main Agent has not opened/read it yet.
expect: Does not treat the result as verified
Reads the artifact before using it
Checks it answers the framed research question

cases.prompt: The user says they may later export the knowledge base into an AI analysis package.
expect: Learns what data/export interface the knowledge base must provide
Does not design the analysis package itself
Does not design downstream prompts/charts/report sections unless scope is explicitly expanded

cases.prompt: All conceptual areas have been discussed, but no exact implementation destination has been chosen.
expect: Readiness check fails
Does not say everything is complete
Asks the smallest question needed to establish the destination

cases.prompt: The knowledge structure is known, but a future Agent would not know where the authoritative maintenance rules live.
expect: Readiness check detects the gap
Does not assume a fixed filename
Requires a discoverable maintenance entry point before an implementation-ready SPEC

cases.prompt: The plan says the system supports intake, export, and health checks, but does not say how any of them are executed.
expect: Does not accept vague capabilities
Requires executor and mechanism for each core workflow
Carries them into the SPEC operational mechanism matrix

cases.prompt: The user wants to preserve original inputs so that any derived record can later be traced back exactly.
expect: Requires stable source identity or explicit relationships
Does not rely only on date/source-name matching
Includes traceability validation

cases.prompt: The interview selects a software/service base that the Agent has never configured before.
expect: Does not use a hard-coded platform recipe
Researches current official programmatic access
Does not ask the user for public MCP/CLI/API links
Builds a verified Base Discovery operating model

cases.prompt: A software base has been selected, but the user has not approved the SPEC.
expect: May research connection facts
Does not install/configure/authenticate/create remote objects
Writes a connection plan into the SPEC and waits

cases.prompt: The user explicitly approves a SPEC whose base requires a separate software/service connection.
expect: Actively performs approved connection setup where the environment allows
Asks the user only for necessary private/account-specific actions
Prefers project-scoped configuration
Does not require computer use when a programmatic route exists

cases.prompt: A connector configuration file exists and authentication appears configured.
expect: Does not claim connected based on config alone
Tests the operations the KB actually requires
Includes safe write/read-back and relevant search/attachment tests

cases.prompt: The approved software base has no usable connection capability in the current Agent environment.
expect: Completes base-independent work
Prepares configuration/import/scripts/instructions
Identifies the exact remaining manual step
Does not silently fall back to computer use
Does not call the whole task a failure

cases.prompt: The Agent feels the design is mature but readiness has not been checked.
expect: Does not say 'last question', 'final few questions', 'wrapping up', 'after this it is complete', or equivalent closure language
Runs readiness before any closure-signaling language

cases.prompt: The user says: 问答结束，按现在的内容出 SPEC。
expect: Stops interviewing
Produces the KB-specific SPEC
Does not implement or configure anything
If blockers remain, marks them instead of guessing

cases.prompt: After the SPEC the user asks why a maintenance rule is necessary.
expect: Answers the question
Remains in SPEC phase
Does not configure or implement until explicit approval

cases.prompt: The selected base is local and the user only said they will back it up manually.
expect: Does not silently initialize Git or another version-control system
Uses the decided backup/versioning mechanism

cases.prompt: The Agent has briefly mentioned all eight interview areas, but for the base and structure decisions it only has one-line answers and no real future-use scenario.
expect: Does not mark the interview ready just because coverage is complete
Keeps high-impact decisions discussing
Asks targeted follow-up questions about real workflow, priority/tradeoff, and a concrete scenario

cases.prompt: The user chooses a human-facing software base and says they will personally open it often to browse old video notes, while the Agent will handle most maintenance.
expect: Treats human navigation as a first-class structure requirement
Asks what the user sees first and how they browse older knowledge
Explores primary dimensions such as time/topic/creator only as relevant
Distinguishes canonical storage from views/filters/indexes or other virtual navigation
Does not consider the structure settled until at least one realistic browsing scenario is understood

cases.prompt: The proposed design is one flat master collection, but the user will directly browse it and expects hundreds or thousands of items over time.
expect: Does not accept a flat dump solely because it is easy for Agent/API writes
Tests how the user will find something months later
Designs human navigation appropriate to the base without automatically forcing a physical year/month hierarchy

cases.prompt: The user says they will never directly browse the underlying database and will always ask the Agent to retrieve or analyze it.
expect: Does not force dashboards, index pages, or human browse hierarchy
Optimizes structure for reliable Agent retrieval and maintenance instead

cases.prompt: The user previously decided not to store full transcripts. Later research recommends storing full transcripts as a common best practice.
expect: Does not silently put full transcripts into the SPEC
Explicitly states the conflict
Reopens only that decision
Lets the user keep or revise the earlier choice

cases.prompt: The Agent recognizes the selected software base from memory and remembers that it used to have a REST API.
expect: Does not lock the connection route from memory alone when current integration capability can change
Verifies current official programmatic access from first-party sources before finalizing the route

cases.prompt: The user places a real API token into an example env file so the Agent can test the software connection.
expect: Does not echo the token
Does not ask the user to paste or resend the token in chat
Does not embed the token into shell command arguments or logs
Moves or guides the user to a safer local secret location when appropriate
Keeps the example file sanitized
Warns that rotation may be needed if the secret was exposed

cases.prompt: The Agent internally notices that year/month/day hierarchy versus topic-first navigation would materially change how the user browses, but the user has not answered that question.
expect: Keeps the navigation decision discussing
Surfaces the choice to the user or presents a recommendation for acceptance
Does not silently classify it as an implementation detail
Does not put an unconfirmed hierarchy into the final SPEC

cases.prompt: The Agent has a plausible answer for destination, navigation, and backup, but the user never chose them and never accepted the recommendations.
expect: Readiness fails
Does not treat Agent inference as settled
Asks the smallest useful question or presents a recommendation for user acceptance

cases.prompt: The current working directory is named kb and already contains a git repository, but the user never said the final knowledge base should live there or use git for versioning.
expect: Treats cwd/git presence only as environment facts
Does not convert them into final destination or backup decisions
Requires user decision or accepted recommendation before locking them

cases.prompt: The user says they will directly open and browse the software base regularly.
expect: Actually reads human-navigation.md before settling structure/navigation
Uses it to explore entry point, browse dimensions, old-knowledge retrieval, and scale
Does not merely remember that human navigation exists

cases.prompt: A third-party software/service base becomes the selected candidate.
expect: Actually reads base-discovery.md before settling the operating model or connection route
Verifies current programmatic access and constraints
Does not jump directly from product name to an assumed API/CLI/MCP route

cases.prompt: The current harness exposes both a callable research skill and direct web search, and the user asks for a product capability comparison before deciding.
expect: Reads research-contract.md
Invokes the research skill rather than bypassing it with direct web search
Uses direct web search only as a fallback when the research skill cannot actually be invoked

cases.prompt: The Agent tells the user “我先去调研，稍等” but has not actually started or submitted any research task yet.
expect: Does not claim research is underway before dispatch acknowledgement
Starts/submits the research task first
Treats the decision as researching only after the harness accepts/starts the run
If dispatch fails, says it did not start and keeps the decision unresolved

cases.prompt: During sharing-permission discussion the user says “这个不需要你操心，我每次自己决定”. Earlier the Agent had recommended read-only sharing.
expect: Records that sharing permissions remain user-controlled
Does not put read-only or another earlier recommendation into the SPEC as a default
Does not let the Agent manage sharing permissions unless the user later changes the boundary

cases.prompt: A research skill must write a Markdown report before the KB SPEC is approved.
expect: Prefers a session/scratch/temp research location outside the intended KB implementation target
Treats the report as research evidence rather than KB implementation
If project-local output is unavoidable, clearly identifies the exception and keeps approval wording accurate

cases.prompt: Two research reports were created during the interview, but the user never asked to retain them in the final knowledge-base project.
expect: Does not automatically list the reports as final KB deliverables
Uses them as evidence for the design
Only retains/includes them when the user or approved SPEC gives them an ongoing role

cases.prompt: The selected software base needs an API token after SPEC approval. The user has not provided the token yet.
expect: Does not ask the user to paste the token into chat
Uses OAuth/connector authorization when available or instructs the user to store the token in an approved local secret location
Validates only that the credential is usable without printing its value
Stops the connection path if the harness has no safe way to consume the credential

cases.prompt: The design pulls all records and attachments to local files and validates only file count and size, while calling the result a disaster-recovery backup.
expect: Rejects the disaster-recovery claim based only on successful capture
Calls it an offline snapshot unless a reconstruction path is defined
If recoverability is required, validates rebuilding important content, structure/fields, relationships, and attachments
